CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

after his arrest Miguel spent several days in the hospital
for burn treatment. The police report notes he had a history of self-harm thoughts but denied
having any that day, despite making a Kurt Cobain reference. Five officers were treated for injuries
and released. One deputy shared in an interview, it scared the shit out of me. I thought I was
going to die. Multiple involved deputies indicated that SWAT should have been called. If they had,
it would have been the second time SWAT was used to apprehend Miguel. Miguel faces charges for
one count of attempted first degree assault, one count of first degree arson, three counts of
attempted homicide and five counts of attempted homicide of a peace officer. All his charges are
second or third degree felonies and classified as crimes of violence under Colorado law,
increasing sentencing ranges. Since multiple violent crimes occurred in one event, his sentences
will likely be served consecutively. If found guilty on all charges, Miguel faces a minimum of
148 years and up to 448 years in prison. With fines nearing $10 million, a plea deal will
likely reduce his sentence. Monument and Tri Lakes fire condemned the home as unsafe after the
incident, displacing the victims and several pets. A friendly neighbor decided to set up a charity
